title: bug: daemon `npm run build` deletes dist/ before its generators run, so a build that fails from WSL left the live daemon with no dist on disk
description:
Found 2026-10-30 18:42Z by the governor. D:\projexts\moes\packages\moe-daemon\dist did not exist, and the gap dates from about 15:31Z (the packages/moe-daemon directory mtime). The live supervisor (pid 13744) and _run (pid 17468, eb0ebaa, started 06:07Z) run from that dist. They kept going only because the code was already loaded. Any _run crash would have hit a supervisor respawn of a missing module: 5 failures in 60s and the board down. The governor restored dist from a clean eb0ebaa staging build at 18:45Z (byte-identical, `status` smoke OK). The daemon was not restarted.

Mechanism (reproduced read-only from WSL in the shared checkout):
- package.json `prebuild` = `npm run clean && npm run generate-init-files && npm run generate-skill-files`. `clean` rmSyncs dist FIRST.
- The shared checkout's node_modules are a Windows install. From WSL, `npx tsx scripts/generate-init-files.ts` exits 1. `npx tsc` throws "Unable to resolve @typescript/typescript-linux-x64": TypeScript here is the native-compiler build, and only the win32-x64 platform package is installed.
- So `npm run build` from any WSL seat in the shared checkout deletes dist and then fails. Open plans whose gates do exactly that are WT-03b (9eae3377), WT-16 (48f0b3aa) and CQ-I06 (4e412148). Governor comments on those rows redirect them to an isolated snapshot.

Fix: make a failed build leave the existing dist alone. Minimum: run both generators before clean, so clean is the last prebuild step right before tsc. tsc emits despite type errors (noEmitOnError is unset), so a type error still rebuilds dist. A stronger variant is allowed if it stays small: tsc into a temp outDir, then rename.
definitionOfDone: packages/moe-daemon/package.json: a build whose generators fail leaves an existing dist/ untouched. At minimum, `prebuild` runs generate-init-files and generate-skill-files BEFORE clean. Windows `npm run build` in a clean clone still produces a complete dist, and the regenerated initFiles.ts/skillFiles.ts stay byte-identical (git status --porcelain empty afterwards).

A test in packages/moe-daemon (vitest) pins the ordering. It reads package.json and fails if `clean` (or any rm of dist) can run before both generators succeed. It is proven RED by a scratch mutant that restores the old order.

Evidence that the failure mode is gone: in a scratch COPY (never the shared checkout) holding a marker file at dist/.keep, running `npm run build` where the generators fail (for example from WSL against Windows-native node_modules) exits non-zero AND dist/.keep still exists. `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0 fresh in a Linux snapshot (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate).
taskRails: Never run `npm run build`, `npm run clean`, `npm ci` or `npm install` in the shared checkout D:\projexts\moes (or /mnt/d/projexts/moes). The live daemon runs from its packages/moe-daemon/dist. Use a git archive or clone snapshot outside the repo for every build or verification step.
Scope: packages/moe-daemon/package.json plus one small test file; no other package, no launcher, no CI change.

implementationPlan.description:
TEST FIRST (RED). Create packages/moe-daemon/src/util/buildScriptOrder.test.ts (~80 lines; helpers stay in the test file, no production module). Header comment: the running daemon loads its modules from dist/, so `npm run build` must fail BEFORE anything deletes dist when a generator or the compiler cannot run (task-f9789178: a WSL build against the Windows-native node_modules deleted the live dist). Read the scripts the way src/server/McpAdapter.test.ts:109 reads the manifest: fs.readFileSync(new URL('../../package.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8').
Helpers:
(a) splitSteps(name, body): scan the body tracking single and double quotes; split on && outside quotes; throw `npm script "<name>" chains steps with "<op>"; only && stops the next step after a failure` for ; | || or a lone & outside quotes (cmd.exe runs the command after a lone & even when the first one failed).
(b) runOrder(scripts, name, depth = 0): the leaf commands `npm run <name>` executes, in order: the steps of pre<name>, then <name>, then post<name> (a missing script adds nothing). A step that is exactly `npm run <x>` or `npm run-script <x>` expands to runOrder(scripts, x, depth + 1), because npm runs x's own pre/post hooks too. Throw past depth 8.
(c) orderViolations(scripts): string[] over runOrder(scripts, 'build'); a thrown error becomes the only violation. Classify leaves: generator = contains scripts/generate-init-files.ts (resp. scripts/generate-skill-files.ts); probe = exactly `tsc --version` or `tsc -v`; emit = `tsc` or `tsc <args>` that is not the probe; removal = a whole-word, case-insensitive rmSync | rmdirSync | rimraf | rm | rmdir | del | rd | Remove-Item AND a `dist` path token (dist bounded by start/end, whitespace, a quote, a paren, a comma or a path separator). Violations, exact wording: 'generate-init-files never runs', 'generate-skill-files never runs', 'tsc --version never runs', 'nothing removes dist' (clean must still run so outputs of deleted sources do not linger; this also stops the order check from passing vacuously if the removal pattern ever misses), 'tsc never emits', `"<leaf>" removes dist before the generators and the compiler probe succeed` for each removal indexed before the last generator/probe, and 'tsc emits before dist is removed' when the emit precedes the last removal.
Error handling: splitSteps and runOrder throw descriptive errors (the offending script and operator; the recursion depth), orderViolations reports a thrown error as its single violation rather than crashing the suite, and an unreadable or invalid package.json fails the test with the fs/JSON error.
Cases: (1) the real scripts -> toEqual([]). (2) it.each over { ...real, ...override }, each asserting toContainEqual(expect.stringContaining(needle)):
- prebuild 'npm run clean && npm run generate-init-files && npm run generate-skill-files' (HEAD's old order) -> 'removes dist before'
- prebuild 'npm run generate-init-files && npm run generate-skill-files; tsc --version && npm run clean' -> 'chains steps with ";"'
- prebuild without `tsc --version && ` -> 'tsc --version never runs'
- prebuild without ` && npm run clean` -> 'nothing removes dist'
- prebuild undefined, build `node -e "require('fs').rmSync('dist',{recursive:true,force:true})" && npm run generate-init-files && npm run generate-skill-files && tsc --version && tsc` -> 'removes dist before'
- prebuild without clean, build 'tsc && npm run clean' -> 'emits before'
The planner prototyped this classification against the real manifest and these rows; it separates them exactly as listed. The project's globalRails forbiddenPatterns apply to the test file too, comments and strings included.
RED: in a Linux snapshot built per step 4 with ONLY this test overlaid (package.json still HEAD's), run `env -i HOME=$HOME NO_COLOR=1 PATH=/home/sysadmin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin npx vitest run src/util/buildScriptOrder.test.ts` from its packages/moe-daemon: case (1) fails naming the clean step, and every row passes. Never run npm in /mnt/d/projexts/moes (task rail).

implementationPlan.description:
FIX. packages/moe-daemon/package.json: change ONLY scripts.prebuild to `npm run generate-init-files && npm run generate-skill-files && tsc --version && npm run clean`. Every other byte stays (clean, build = tsc, both generator scripts, 2-space JSON, LF, final newline); `git diff packages/moe-daemon/package.json` shows one -/+ line pair.
Order rationale (repeat it in the step note): generators first, so a generator failure (WSL tsx/esbuild against win32 node_modules) stops the chain before clean. Clean last, right before build's tsc, so stale outputs of deleted sources are still removed and a type error still rebuilds dist (noEmitOnError unset).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Chosen: prebuild = generators, then `tsc --version`, then clean. It is one line and adds no new failure mode. (2) Reorder only (the row's stated minimum). It leaves the second half of the governor's repro open: once the generators no longer depend on tsx, a tsc that cannot resolve its native platform package would delete dist again. node >= 22.18 can run them by type stripping, since they import only node builtins. The probe costs one native exec. (3) tsc into a temp outDir, then rename. Rejected: Windows has no atomic directory swap, so it is still rm + rename, and renaming freshly written trees fails with EPERM/EBUSY under AV or indexers. It is also more moving parts than a scope-railed row allows. (4) Drop clean. Rejected: outputs of deleted sources would linger in dist, the npm package and the IDE bundles.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: npm runs prebuild, then build, then postbuild, and it also runs the pre/post hooks of a nested `npm run x`. cmd.exe and sh treat && the same way, but cmd treats a lone & like ;. The generators never read or write dist. At HEAD 77e9e47c, a generator run in a full clone reproduced src/generated byte-identically, so DoD 1's empty-porcelain check is achievable. A git archive has no history and changes initFiles.ts's shipped-body list, so DoD 1 needs a real Windows git clone. TypeScript 7's bin/tsc resolves the native binary before parsing args, so `tsc --version` is a real startability probe. moe-proxy and moe-claude-plugin have the same clean-first prebuild, and the launchers run packages/moe-proxy/dist/index.js. Both are out of this row's scope (rail) and flagged to the governor.
planningNotes.risks: Any npm build in /mnt/d/projexts/moes deletes or replaces the live daemon's dist. Every build runs in $W or $SNAP behind `cd <dir> || exit 1`. With WSL interop, call cmd.exe only from a /mnt/d cwd and strip \r before diffing. Peer WIP checkpoints can turn the full suite red at HEAD: prove it with a plain-HEAD archive and block on the owning row; never edit their files.
